indexScope: Curated 1900-2000 reference material for a game that may diverge. Not a claim of complete coverage.
note: Events are real-world references. The simulator may use them as weights, conditions or candidate hooks, but must commit its own world-local events with their own causes and outcomes.

records.title: Rapid population growth in Vienna
records.summary: Vienna’s population grew rapidly around 1900 through immigration from Bohemia, Moravia, Galicia and the Balkans, producing housing shortages and a diverse urban society.
records.inferenceNote: Aggregate trend, not a single dated event. The exact population figures depend on census boundaries and are not asserted here.

records.title: Federation of Australia
records.summary: Six British colonies federated as the Commonwealth of Australia, a self-governing dominion within the British Empire.

records.title: Wednesday Psychological Society begins meeting in Vienna
records.summary: Sigmund Freud’s Wednesday evening discussion circle began meeting at Berggasse 19 in October 1902; it was reconstituted as the Vienna Psychoanalytic Society in 1908.

records.title: Russo-Japanese War
records.summary: Japan and Russia fought over Manchuria and Korea; Japan’s victory unsettled assumptions of European military supremacy in Asia.

records.title: Russian Revolution of 1905
records.summary: Bloody Sunday in St Petersburg triggered strikes, peasant unrest and mutinies, forcing Tsar Nicholas II to concede a parliament and civil liberties.

records.title: Universal male suffrage adopted in Cisleithania
records.summary: The Austrian half of Austria-Hungary adopted universal male suffrage for elections to the Imperial Council; the 1907 election followed in May.

records.title: Austro-Hungarian annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
records.summary: Austria-Hungary formally annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina, which it had occupied since 1878, triggering a major European crisis with Serbia and Russia.

records.title: Xinhai Revolution
records.summary: The Wuchang uprising spread into a revolution that ended the Qing dynasty and established the Republic of China.

records.title: First Balkan War
records.summary: The Balkan League attacked the Ottoman Empire and drove it from most of its European territories, creating an independent Albania and escalating great-power rivalry.

records.title: Second Balkan War
records.summary: Bulgaria attacked Serbia and Greece over the division of Macedonia and was defeated by a wider coalition, leaving the Balkan order unstable.

records.title: July Crisis
records.summary: A sequence of ultimatums, mobilizations and declarations of war turned a Balkan crisis into a general European war.

records.title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo
records.summary: Gavrilo Princip shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand and Sophie in Sarajevo, setting off the July Crisis and, within weeks, World War I.

records.title: World War I
records.summary: The First World War industrialized mass slaughter, destroyed four empires and redrew the map of Europe and the Middle East.

records.title: Armenian genocide
records.summary: The Ottoman government deported and murdered Armenians in a systematic genocide during World War I; the death toll and legal characterization remain contested by Turkey.

records.title: Death of Emperor Franz Joseph I
records.summary: Emperor Franz Joseph died in Vienna after 68 years on the throne; Charles I inherited a monarchy increasingly dependent on Germany.

records.title: Battle of the Somme
records.summary: A massive British and French offensive on the Western Front produced enormous casualties with limited territorial gain, becoming a symbol of attrition warfare.

records.title: February Revolution in Russia
records.summary: Food protests and strikes in Petrograd escalated into the collapse of the tsarist regime and the formation of a provisional government.

records.title: October Revolution
records.summary: The Bolsheviks seized power in Petrograd, leading to Soviet Russia, civil war and a new model of revolutionary politics across Europe.

records.title: United States enters World War I
records.summary: The United States declared war on Germany after unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram, tipping the military balance toward the Allies.

records.title: Influenza reaches Vienna
records.summary: The 1918 influenza pandemic hit Vienna amid food shortages, military collapse and the birth of the republic; local mortality and institutional responses varied.
records.inferenceNote: The global pandemic is documented; the precise Vienna wave timing and death toll are synthesized from secondary accounts and should be checked against local archives.

records.title: Austro-Hungarian armistice
records.summary: Austria-Hungary signed an armistice with Italy at Villa Giusti, ending its participation in World War I.

records.title: Czechoslovak declaration of independence
records.summary: The Czechoslovak National Council declared independence in Prague as Austria-Hungary disintegrated after World War I.

records.title: Republic of German-Austria declared
records.summary: The provisional National Assembly in Vienna declared German-Austria a republic, one day after the Habsburg emperor renounced participation in government.

records.title: 1918 influenza pandemic
records.summary: The H1N1 influenza pandemic spread worldwide in three waves, killing an estimated tens of millions and overwhelming health services and wartime logistics.

records.title: Armistice of 11 November 1918
records.summary: Germany signed the armistice at Compiègne, ending fighting on the Western Front and bringing World War I to a close.

records.title: Postwar housing crisis in Vienna
records.summary: Returning soldiers, refugees and the collapse of the Habsburg housing market produced severe overcrowding in Vienna, setting the stage for the later municipal housing programme.
records.inferenceNote: A synthesized condition rather than a discrete event; exact dates of shortage peaks are uncertain.

records.title: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye
records.summary: The peace treaty with Austria confirmed the dissolution of Austria-Hungary, recognized the successor states and restricted Austrian union with Germany.

records.title: Treaty of Versailles
records.summary: The peace treaty with Germany imposed territorial losses, disarmament, reparations and war-guilt clauses, reshaping European politics for decades.

records.title: Austrian Federal Constitution adopted
records.summary: The Austrian Federal Constitutional Law established the First Republic’s federal parliamentary system; it remains the basis of Austrian constitutional law.

records.title: League of Nations founded
records.summary: The League of Nations began work after World War I; the United States never joined, limiting its authority.

records.title: League of Nations loan to Austria
records.summary: Austria accepted League of Nations financial supervision and a loan in exchange for austerity, stabilizing the currency but deepening political conflict.

records.title: March on Rome
records.summary: Mussolini’s Fascists staged a mass march on Rome and were handed power by the king, establishing the first Fascist government in Europe.

records.title: Beer Hall Putsch
records.summary: Hitler and the Nazis attempted a coup in Munich; it failed, but the trial and publicity helped build the movement.

records.title: July Revolt in Vienna
records.summary: After a controversial acquittal, a mass protest in Vienna ended with the burning of the Palace of Justice and police shootings; the conflict deepened the divide between Social Democrats and the right.

records.title: Wall Street Crash
records.summary: The New York stock market collapsed, triggering a global depression, mass unemployment and political radicalization.

records.title: Depression-era unemployment in Austria
records.summary: The global Depression hit Austrian industry and banking hard, producing mass unemployment and support for radical political movements before the 1938 Anschluss.
records.inferenceNote: Aggregate condition; unemployment statistics for the period are contested and are not reproduced here.

records.title: Creditanstalt banking crisis
records.summary: The collapse of Vienna’s Creditanstalt bank triggered a Central European banking panic and deepened the Depression.

records.title: Hitler appointed German chancellor
records.summary: President Hindenburg appointed Adolf Hitler chancellor; within months the Nazi regime dismantled the Weimar democracy.

records.title: Austrian Civil War
records.summary: Government forces shelled Social Democratic housing estates and suppressed the Schutzbund, ending the First Republic’s democratic order.

records.title: Assassination of Engelbert Dollfuss
records.summary: Austrian Nazis assassinated Chancellor Dollfuss during a failed putsch; Kurt Schuschnigg succeeded him.

records.title: Nuremberg Laws
records.summary: The Nazi regime stripped German Jews of citizenship and criminalized relationships deemed racially unacceptable, institutionalizing antisemitic persecution.

records.title: Spanish Civil War
records.summary: A military uprising against the Second Republic became a civil war involving Nazi Germany, Fascist Italy and the Soviet Union, and a rehearsal for World War II.

records.title: Anschluss: Austria annexed by Nazi Germany
records.summary: German troops entered Austria and the country was incorporated into the German Reich, accompanied by mass persecution of Jews and political opponents.

records.title: Kristallnacht pogrom
records.summary: Nazi-organized pogroms destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses across Germany and annexed Austria; tens of thousands of Jewish men were arrested.

records.title: World War II
records.summary: The Second World War began with the German invasion of Poland and became a global war of conquest, occupation, genocide and mass bombing; it ended with the defeat of Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan.

records.title: Fall of France
records.summary: France signed an armistice with Germany after a rapid German offensive; the country was divided into occupied and Vichy zones.

records.title: Operation Barbarossa
records.summary: Nazi Germany invaded the Soviet Union, opening the largest land front in history and enabling mass murder of Jews and prisoners of war.

records.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
records.summary: Japan attacked the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, bringing the United States into World War II and widening the conflict into a global war.

records.title: Battle of Stalingrad
records.summary: The encirclement and surrender of the German Sixth Army at Stalingrad marked a turning point on the Eastern Front.

records.title: Wannsee Conference
records.summary: Nazi officials coordinated the implementation of the “Final Solution,” the systematic murder of European Jews.

records.title: Normandy landings
records.summary: Allied forces landed in Normandy, opening the Western Front and beginning the liberation of German-occupied Western Europe.

records.title: Warsaw Uprising
records.summary: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupation; the uprising was crushed and Warsaw was largely destroyed.

records.title: Food and fuel crisis in occupied Vienna
records.summary: Vienna faced severe food, fuel and housing shortages after the fighting, with a damaged economy and a population coping with occupation and displacement.
records.inferenceNote: A synthesized period condition; local supply varied by district and by occupation zone.

records.title: German Instrument of Surrender
records.summary: Germany surrendered unconditionally, ending World War II in Europe and opening the occupation and division of the country.

records.title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
records.summary: The United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, killing tens of thousands and precipitating Japan’s surrender.

records.title: Nuremberg trials
records.summary: The Allied powers tried Nazi leaders for crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity, establishing a landmark in international criminal law.

records.title: Second Austrian Republic proclaimed
records.summary: A provisional government in Vienna declared the Second Republic and restored the 1920 constitution, while Allied occupation forces controlled Austria.

records.title: United Nations founded
records.summary: The United Nations Charter entered into force, creating a new global organization with a Security Council and specialized agencies.

records.title: Vienna Offensive
records.summary: Soviet forces captured Vienna after heavy fighting; the city was badly damaged and the Nazi regime collapsed in Austria.

records.title: Truman Doctrine
records.summary: The United States pledged support to governments resisting communism, marking a decisive turn toward containment in the Cold War.

records.title: Berlin Blockade and airlift
records.summary: The Soviet Union blocked road and rail access to West Berlin; the Western Allies supplied the city by air until the blockade was lifted.

records.title: Marshall Plan
records.summary: The United States funded European reconstruction through the European Recovery Program, stabilizing economies and deepening the East-West divide.

records.title: North Atlantic Treaty signed
records.summary: The North Atlantic Treaty created a collective defence alliance linking the United States and Western Europe against Soviet power.

records.title: People’s Republic of China proclaimed
records.summary: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People’s Republic of China after the Communist victory in the civil war; the Nationalist government retreated to Taiwan.

records.title: Korean War
records.summary: North Korea invaded South Korea; a UN-led coalition intervened, China entered the war, and the conflict ended in an armistice without a peace treaty.

records.title: Death of Joseph Stalin
records.summary: Stalin died in Moscow, triggering a succession struggle, de-Stalinization and unrest across the Soviet bloc.

records.title: Austrian Declaration of Neutrality
records.summary: Austria’s parliament declared permanent neutrality, a constitutional commitment that shaped the Second Republic’s Cold War role.

records.title: Austrian State Treaty
records.summary: Austria and the four occupying powers signed the State Treaty, restoring Austrian sovereignty and ending the postwar occupation.

records.title: Hungarian refugees arrive in Austria
records.summary: After the Soviet suppression of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution, roughly 200,000 people fled Hungary; Austria received a large share and organized emergency reception and resettlement.
records.inferenceNote: The refugee flow is well documented; the exact number assisted in Austria varies by source and period.

records.title: Hungarian Revolution
records.summary: A nationwide uprising against communist rule and Soviet domination was crushed by Soviet forces; hundreds of thousands fled, many to Austria.

records.title: Treaty of Rome
records.summary: Six European states created the European Economic Community and Euratom, founding the institutional core of what became the European Union.

records.title: Berlin Wall built
records.summary: East Germany sealed the border between East and West Berlin, building a wall that became the symbol of the Cold War division of Europe.

records.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
records.summary: The discovery of Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba brought the United States and the Soviet Union to the brink of nuclear war before a negotiated withdrawal.

records.title: Czechoslovak refugees after the Prague Spring
records.summary: The Warsaw Pact invasion prompted thousands of Czechoslovaks to flee west; Austria again became a first country of asylum and transit.
records.inferenceNote: A synthesized migration period; precise counts and duration of stay require archival verification.

records.title: Prague Spring
records.summary: Alexander Dubček’s Czechoslovak reforms promised “socialism with a human face,” sparking cultural and political liberalization before the Warsaw Pact invasion.

records.title: Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia
records.summary: Soviet-led Warsaw Pact forces invaded Czechoslovakia, ending the Prague Spring and enforcing the Brezhnev Doctrine.

records.title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
records.summary: Apollo 11 landed humans on the Moon, a landmark of spaceflight, engineering and Cold War prestige competition.

records.title: Munich massacre
records.summary: Palestinian militants killed Israeli athletes at the Munich Olympics; the crisis exposed the vulnerability of public events and shaped counterterrorism.

records.title: 1973 oil crisis
records.summary: Arab oil producers embargoed countries supporting Israel during the Yom Kippur War, quadrupling oil prices and triggering inflation and recession.

records.title: Helsinki Accords
records.summary: The Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe adopted the Helsinki Final Act, linking détente with human-rights commitments that later empowered dissidents.

records.title: Solidarity founded in Poland
records.summary: The Gdańsk shipyard strikes produced Solidarity, the first independent mass trade union in the Soviet bloc, challenging communist party monopoly.

records.title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
records.summary: A reactor explosion at Chernobyl released radioactive material across Europe, exposing the limits of Soviet secrecy and nuclear safety.

records.title: Opening of Austria’s eastern borders
records.summary: The collapse of the Iron Curtain transformed Austria’s eastern border from a fortified frontier into a zone of cross-border traffic, labour migration and new regional integration.
records.inferenceNote: Aggregate transition; exact dates differ by border crossing and by the collapse of the Hungarian and Czechoslovak regimes.

records.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
records.summary: East Germany opened the Berlin Wall after mass protests and border reforms, symbolizing the collapse of the Cold War division of Europe.

records.title: Romanian Revolution
records.summary: Protests and a military uprising ended the Ceausescu dictatorship; the dictator and his wife were executed on 25 December.

records.title: Tiananmen Square protests and massacre
records.summary: Student-led protests for reform were crushed by the military in Beijing, with a death toll that remains officially disputed.

records.title: Velvet Revolution
records.summary: Mass protests in Prague and other cities ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia and brought Václav Havel to the presidency.

records.title: German reunification
records.summary: The German Democratic Republic joined the Federal Republic of Germany, ending the division of Germany within the larger collapse of the Soviet bloc.

records.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
records.summary: The Soviet Union formally dissolved into fifteen independent republics, ending the Cold War bipolar order.

records.title: Yugoslav Wars
records.summary: The violent breakup of Yugoslavia produced wars in Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia, with ethnic cleansing, sieges and international intervention.

records.title: Bosnian War
records.summary: War in Bosnia followed the republic’s independence declaration, involving Bosnian government forces, Serb and Croat forces, ethnic cleansing and international intervention.

records.title: Maastricht Treaty
records.summary: The Maastricht Treaty created the European Union and set the path toward a single currency and common foreign and security policy.

records.title: Dissolution of Czechoslovakia
records.summary: Czechoslovakia divided peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia after political negotiations.

records.title: Austria joins the European Union
records.summary: Austria became a member of the European Union after a 1994 referendum, ending its postwar policy of non-membership in the European Communities.

records.title: Dayton Agreement
records.summary: The Dayton Agreement ended the Bosnian War and created a complex federal state with international supervision.

records.title: Srebrenica massacre
records.summary: Bosnian Serb forces murdered more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys after the UN safe area of Srebrenica fell, the worst atrocity in Europe since World War II.

records.title: Kosovo War
records.summary: NATO bombed Yugoslavia to stop the campaign against Kosovo Albanians; the war ended with a NATO-led protectorate and a lasting sovereignty dispute.

records.title: Austrian Freedom Party enters government
records.summary: The conservative People’s Party formed a coalition with the far-right Freedom Party, prompting EU sanctions and a debate about Austria’s postwar self-image.
